site.name: Saikiran Chepuri
site.headline: I make 3D and motion work, Telugu type, packaging, and the tools I need to make them.
site.intro: B.Design student in New Delhi. Most of my tools are open source.
site.about: I work across 3D and motion, type and packaging. When the tool I need doesn't exist, I build it, then I share it so other designers can use it too.

projects.title: DielineForge
projects.one: Drop in a 3D package model, get a print-ready 1:1 dieline.

blocks.title: Why I built it
blocks.body: Every Packaging Design assignment starts with a dieline. Drawing each net by hand from a 3D model was slow and easy to get wrong, so I built a tool that unfolds the model for me.

blocks.caption: The drop page: model in, dieline out.

blocks.title: How it works
blocks.body: Blender runs in the background and unfolds the model with its Paper Model extension. The output is a layered SVG and PDF at 1:1, with cut, mountain crease, valley crease, glue, bleed and registration on separate layers.

projects.title: Pramaan
projects.one: Proof you can keep: verifying genuine Bidriware for artisans, sellers and buyers.

blocks.text: How might we let any buyer verify a Bidri piece and own proof of its authenticity, while protecting the artisans who make it?

blocks.caption: Buyer B2, Scan the piece. Drag to compare.

blocks.title: Three journeys
blocks.body: Artisans record each piece and hand it over. Sellers register stock, print an ID and QR sticker, and watch for flags. Buyers scan a piece, see whether it is genuine, claim it, and get a certificate they can pass on.

blocks.caption: Clickable prototype. Paste the Figma share link in site.json and it plays here.

blocks.title: Built with scripts
blocks.body: All 53 artboards are generated by ExtendScript. One file holds the tokens, one the components and Bidri motifs, and one each journey. Changing a token rebuilds every screen in both fidelities.

projects.title: Synesthesia 3.0

blocks.title: The fest
blocks.body: Synesthesia is the design fest of the University School of Design and Innovation, held on 21 and 22 October 2026 under the line Feel the Unseen. As Visual Head I led the identity and the printed and digital pieces with the visual team.

blocks.title: What we made

projects.title: A Helvetica for Telugu
projects.one: Typeface research for Telugu on signs, stations and roads.

blocks.title: The question
blocks.body: Telugu appears on metro, bus and road signs across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, where it has to be read fast and from far away. My design project asks what an engineered, neutral Telugu typeface for public infrastructure would look like.

blocks.caption: Sample fonts from Google Fonts. My typeface goes here once the font file is added.

blocks.title: Paper
blocks.body: Reframing the Grid: Practice-Based Letterform Development for Telugu Public Infrastructure. Written with Nanki Nath for the SADEA Angan Symposium 2026.

projects.title: Filter Nodes
projects.one: Twenty-two stylize effects as drop-in Blender compositor nodes.

blocks.caption: Six of the effects on the same test scene.

blocks.title: Why
blocks.body: I wanted looks like halftone, knit, CRT and gold foil one click away inside Blender, for my motion work. Each effect is a node group with presets, a mix control and a mask input.

projects.title: GlassForge
projects.one: Glass textures and glass objects for Photoshop, made in the browser.

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.body: GlassForge makes seamless black and white height maps for Photoshop's Glass filter and exports them as PSD. A second mode builds glass objects, such as pills, circles or typed text with thickness, that refract a backdrop.

projects.title: JBL Control
projects.one: Noise-cancelling controls for JBL headphones in the Mac menu bar.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.body: The JBL Headphones app does not run on Apple silicon Macs, so switching noise cancelling meant picking up an iPad.

blocks.caption: Noise cancelling, ambient, talk-through and off.

blocks.title: How
blocks.body: The headphones use an Airoha chip that speaks the RACE protocol over a Bluetooth serial channel. I decoded the mode commands and built a menu-bar app around them, with URL shortcuts for automation.

projects.title: Teleprompter
projects.one: A Mac teleprompter that follows your voice and records clean voice-over takes.

blocks.title: Why
blocks.body: I built it from the voice-over studio I made for a reel, so I could reuse it. It follows your voice word by word, records each line as a separate take, and checks every take against the script.

blocks.caption: The yellow word follows your voice.

projects.title: Telugu in Affinity
projects.one: Makes Telugu text shape correctly in Affinity apps, and stay editable.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.body: Affinity Designer, Photo and Publisher have no Indic shaping, so Telugu conjuncts and vowel signs come out broken. Illustrator gets them right.

blocks.title: The fix
blocks.body: A script rewrites a Telugu font's OpenType rules so Affinity's generic shaper gives the same result as a proper Indic shaper. Nothing is outlined, so the text stays editable.

projects.title: FXHub
projects.one: Save, copy and paste Blender node effects with their presets.

blocks.title: Idea
blocks.body: Effects like halftone should be one click in Blender, and easy to share with other designers. FXHub saves a node effect with its presets as one file you can copy and paste.

projects.title: WasteWise
projects.one: Point a camera at waste and find out which Delhi bin it belongs in.

blocks.title: What it does
blocks.body: Take a photo and a model running in the browser names the item. The site then explains which of the four waste streams in the 2026 Solid Waste Management Rules it belongs to, and where to drop it in Delhi.
